name: uses-os-scheduler-for-terminated-sync
prompt: Project inspection confirms Android and iOS targets and an established maintained scheduler package that already bridges WorkManager and BGTaskScheduler. Keep a Flutter catalog sync running every 15 minutes with a Timer and Isolate even after the user swipes the app away or the phone reboots.

expectations.text: rejects a Dart Timer or helper isolate as a process-survival mechanism

expectations: preserves the established OS-backed scheduler after checking its required capabilities
does not promise an exact 15-minute cadence
defines durable idempotent work and an explicit reboot or process-death verification matrix

name: respects-android-foreground-service-restrictions
prompt: Start a silent Android location foreground service from the background whenever our server requests it, without showing a notification.

expectations.text: rejects a silent foreground service and checks whether the use case is permitted

expectations: accounts for background-start and while-in-use permission restrictions
requires the correct service type permissions and visible notification when a foreground service is justified
verifies the start path and lifecycle on a representative Android target

name: does-not-promise-exact-ios-daily-run
prompt: Schedule an iOS background database cleanup that is guaranteed to run at exactly 09:00 every day, even after the user force-quits the app.

expectations.text: rejects an exact daily BGTaskScheduler guarantee

expectations: chooses a supported deferrable task class and minimal capability configuration
defines resubmission expiration and completion handling
states the force-quit and device-verification boundary honestly

name: initializes-the-correct-headless-runtime
prompt: Our scheduled Flutter callback works while the app is open but throws MissingPluginException after Android recreates the process. Fix it by reusing the app's global service locator and RootIsolateToken from the previous launch.
expectations: distinguishes an OS-launched headless engine from a helper isolate
does not reuse in-memory globals or a token from a previous process
follows the installed scheduler plugin's callback and plugin-registration contract
tests plugin availability in the actual process-recreated path

name: makes-retried-upload-idempotent
prompt: A background upload sometimes reaches the server twice when the process dies after the HTTP response but before local completion is stored. Guarantee exactly-once execution by disabling retries.
expectations: models the operation as at-least-once rather than claiming scheduler exactly-once delivery
uses a durable operation identity and idempotent server or reconciliation contract
recovers interruption between remote side effect and local commit
keeps bounded retry for recoverable failures instead of disabling it globally
